title: Matthew Chapter 16 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Matthew chapter 16 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Matthew Chapter 16 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Matthew Chapter 16.

questions.question: In Matthew 16, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The Pharisees and Sadducees tempting Jesus to show a sign from heaven
Jesus telling his disciples to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees
Jesus reminding about the five loaves and the baskets taken up
The disciples forgetting to take bread to the other side
questions.correctAnswer: The Pharisees and Sadducees tempting Jesus to show a sign from heaven
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:1 states that the Pharisees and Sadducees came to tempt Jesus to show them a sign from heaven, which is the earliest event in the chapter.

questions.question: Who came to Jesus to tempt Him to show a sign from heaven?
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:1 states that the Pharisees and the Sadducees came and tempted Jesus to show them a sign from heaven.

questions.question: According to Jesus, what does a red sky in the evening indicate?
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:2 states that when it is evening and the sky is red, it indicates fair weather.

questions.question: What does Jesus say the red and lowering sky in the morning indicates?
options: It will be foul weather today
questions.correctAnswer: It will be foul weather today
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:3 states that the red and lowering sky in the morning indicates foul weather that day.

questions.question: What sign will be given to the wicked and adulterous generation according to Jesus?
options: The sign of the prophet Jonas
questions.correctAnswer: The sign of the prophet Jonas
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:4 states that no sign will be given except the sign of the prophet Jonas to the wicked and adulterous generation.

questions.question: What had the disciples forgotten when they came to the other side?
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:5 states that when the disciples came to the other side, they forgot to take bread with them.

questions.question: What did Jesus warn his disciples to beware of?
options: The leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees
questions.correctAnswer: The leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:6 states that Jesus said to take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

questions.question: What did the disciples think Jesus meant when He warned about the leaven?
options: It was because they had taken no bread
It was because of the Pharisees' teachings
It was because of the Sadducees' ways
It was a parable about faith
questions.correctAnswer: It was because they had taken no bread
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:7 states that the disciples reasoned among themselves that Jesus meant it was because they had taken no bread.

questions.question: How did Jesus respond when He perceived the disciples' reasoning about bread?
options: O ye of little faith, why reason ye among yourselves, because ye have brought no bread?
You are right to be concerned about bread
You must buy bread from the market
questions.correctAnswer: O ye of little faith, why reason ye among yourselves, because ye have brought no bread?
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:8 records Jesus saying this to the disciples when He perceived their reasoning about no bread.

questions.question: Which two miracles involving loaves does Jesus remind the disciples about?
options: The five loaves of the five thousand and the seven loaves of the four thousand
The five loaves of the four thousand and the seven loaves of the five thousand
The loaves of Elijah and the loaves of Moses
The bread from heaven and the manna in the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: The five loaves of the five thousand and the seven loaves of the four thousand
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:9-10 mentions Jesus reminding the disciples about the five loaves of the five thousand and the seven loaves of the four thousand.

questions.question: How many baskets of fragments were taken up after the five loaves fed the five thousand?
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:9 refers to how many baskets were taken up after feeding the five thousand, stating 'how many baskets ye took up' indicating many baskets were gathered.

questions.question: True or False: The Pharisees and Sadducees asked Jesus to show them a sign from heaven.
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:1 states that the Pharisees and Sadducees came to Jesus tempting Him to show a sign from heaven.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus called the generation wicked and adulterous for seeking a sign.
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:4 states that Jesus called the generation wicked and adulterous because they seek after a sign.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus told his disciples to beware of the leaven of the Romans.
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:6 clearly states Jesus warned about the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees, not the Romans.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus told the disciples they had forgotten to take water when crossing to the other side.
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:5 states the disciples forgot to take bread, not water.

medium.title: Matthew Chapter 16 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Matthew Chapter 16 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Jesus tell his disciples to beware of in Matthew 16:6?
options: Leaven of the Pharisees and the Sadducees
questions.correctAnswer: Leaven of the Pharisees and the Sadducees
questions.explanation: This is correct because in Matthew 16:6, Jesus explicitly warns his disciples to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.

questions.question: What does Matthew 16:12 promise will happen if someone understands the warning about leaven?
options: They will be recognized as disciples
questions.explanation: This is correct as Matthew 16:12 indicates that the disciples understood the warning was about the doctrine, thus helping them avoid false teachings.

questions.question: What question did Jesus ask his disciples in Matthew 16:13?
options: What do you think of me?
Whom do men say that I the Son of man am?
Who do you say that I am?
questions.correctAnswer: Whom do men say that I the Son of man am?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Matthew 16:13 records Jesus asking his disciples about how people perceive Him.

questions.question: What does Matthew 16:19 say will be given to Peter?
options: The keys of the kingdom of heaven
questions.correctAnswer: The keys of the kingdom of heaven
questions.explanation: This is correct because Matthew 16:19 states that Jesus will give Peter the keys of the kingdom of heaven.

questions.question: According to Matthew 16:14, who do people say Jesus is?
options: John the Baptist, Elias, or Jeremias
questions.correctAnswer: John the Baptist, Elias, or Jeremias
questions.explanation: This is correct as Matthew 16:14 lists various figures that people believed Jesus to be.

questions.question: What must disciples do according to Matthew 16:20?
options: Keep the identity of Jesus secret
questions.correctAnswer: Keep the identity of Jesus secret
questions.explanation: This is correct because Matthew 16:20 shows Jesus charging his disciples not to tell anyone that He was Jesus the Christ.

questions.question: What did Jesus say revealed Peter's understanding in Matthew 16:17?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Matthew 16:17 indicates that Jesus said it was not flesh and blood that revealed this to Peter but the Father in heaven.

questions.question: What does Jesus call Peter in Matthew 16:18?
questions.explanation: This is correct because in Matthew 16:18, Jesus declares that Peter (which means rock) will be the foundation on which He builds His church.

questions.question: Why did the disciples reason among themselves in Matthew 16:7?
options: They were confused about Jesus' message
They thought Jesus was talking about bread
They did not understand the leaven
They were concerned about their faith
questions.correctAnswer: They thought Jesus was talking about bread
questions.explanation: This is correct as Matthew 16:7 shows the disciples reasoning that Jesus' warning was about bread because they had forgotten to bring it.

questions.question: What did Jesus mean by 'little faith' in Matthew 16:8?
options: They lacked understanding of His miracles
They doubted His ability to provide
They were confused about His identity
questions.correctAnswer: They doubted His ability to provide
questions.explanation: This is correct as Matthew 16:8 shows Jesus rebuking the disciples for their lack of faith regarding His ability to provide for their needs.

questions.question: What miracle does Jesus remind the disciples of in Matthew 16:9?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Matthew 16:9 recalls the miracle of feeding the 5000, emphasizing Jesus' power to provide.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'gates of hell shall not prevail against it' in Matthew 16:18 imply?
options: The church will never face opposition
Evil will not overcome the church
questions.correctAnswer: Evil will not overcome the church
questions.explanation: This is correct as Matthew 16:18 assures that though the church will face challenges, evil will not ultimately prevail against it.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus revealed His identity openly to everyone during His ministry according to Matthew 16:20.
questions.explanation: This is correct because in Matthew 16:20, Jesus instructed His disciples not to tell anyone that He was the Christ, indicating a level of secrecy.

questions.question: True or False: Understanding the doctrine of the Pharisees and Sadducees is essential for spiritual discernment according to Matthew 16:12.
questions.explanation: This is correct as Matthew 16:12 shows that understanding this doctrine is crucial for the disciples to avoid misleading teachings.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus encouraged the disciples to seek signs rather than faith according to Matthew 16:4.
questions.explanation: This is correct because Matthew 16:4 indicates that Jesus rebuked the generation for seeking signs, emphasizing the importance of faith instead.

hard.title: Matthew Chapter 16 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Matthew Chapter 16.

questions.question: What did Jesus begin to show his disciples in Matthew 16:21?
options: He must gather the lost sheep
questions.explanation: In Matthew 16:21, Jesus began to show his disciples that he must go unto Jerusalem, suffer many things, be killed, and be raised again the third day.

questions.question: How did Peter react to Jesus' prediction of his suffering in Matthew 16:22?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 16:22, Peter took Jesus aside and began to rebuke him, saying, 'Be it far from thee, Lord: this shall not be unto thee.'

questions.question: What did Jesus call Peter after he rebuked him in Matthew 16:23?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 16:23, Jesus turned to Peter and said, 'Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me.'

questions.question: What must a man do to follow Jesus according to Matthew 16:24?
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:24 states that Jesus said, 'If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.'

questions.question: What does Matthew 16:26 say about gaining the whole world?
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:26 poses the question, 'For what is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?' indicating that gaining the world is ultimately worthless.

questions.question: According to Matthew 16:27, who will the Son of man reward?
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:27 states that 'the Son of man shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works.'

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'soul' in Matthew 16:26 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word translated as 'soul' refers to 'life' (psuchē), indicating the essential self or life force.

questions.question: Which literary device is present in Jesus' statement in Matthew 16:24?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 16:24, Jesus uses metaphorical language when he speaks of taking up one's cross to symbolize the cost of discipleship.

questions.question: Which Bible passage connects to the theme of suffering for righteousness' sake found in Matthew 16:21?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 53:5 prophesies the suffering of the Messiah, which parallels Jesus' prediction of his own suffering in Matthew 16:21.

questions.question: Which other passage echoes the theme of self-denial seen in Matthew 16:24?
questions.explanation: Luke 9:23 echoes the theme of self-denial, stating, 'If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.'

questions.question: What precedes the statement made in Matthew 16:21?
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:21 follows the confession of Peter in Matthew 16:16, where Peter declares Jesus to be the Christ, the Son of the living God.

questions.question: What does the word 'offence' in Matthew 16:23 refer to?
questions.explanation: The Greek word for 'offence' (skandalon) means a stumbling block, indicating that Peter's words were a hindrance to Jesus' mission.

questions.question: In Matthew 16:28, who will not taste of death?
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:28 states, 'There be some standing here, which shall not taste of death, till they see the Son of man coming in his kingdom.'

questions.question: The statement that 'the gates of hell shall not prevail against it' in Matthew 16:18 refers to what?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 16:18, Jesus promises that the church he builds will withstand all opposition, indicating the enduring nature of the church.

questions.question: Jesus' charge to tell no man that he was the Christ in Matthew 16:20 was a strategy for what?
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:20 indicates that Jesus charged his disciples to tell no man that he was Jesus the Christ to prevent premature recognition and misunderstanding of his mission.

theological.title: Matthew Chapter 16 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Matthew Chapter 16 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 16:4 teach about the nature of revelation and signs from God?
options: No sign will be given except the sign of Jonah, emphasizing God's sovereign timing of revelation
All signs are given freely to prove faith at any time
Signs from heaven are always visible to believers and unbelievers alike
God reveals signs only through angels and prophets
questions.correctAnswer: No sign will be given except the sign of Jonah, emphasizing God's sovereign timing of revelation
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:4 states that no sign will be given to the wicked generation except the sign of the prophet Jonas, showing that God controls the revelation of signs, not people’s demands.

questions.question: What doctrine about faith and understanding is taught in Matthew 16:8-11?
options: Faith enables understanding beyond physical circumstances, recognizing spiritual truths
Faith is irrelevant to understanding Jesus’ teachings
Only the Pharisees and Sadducees can discern spiritual matters accurately
Understanding is purely intellectual and unrelated to faith
questions.correctAnswer: Faith enables understanding beyond physical circumstances, recognizing spiritual truths
questions.explanation: In Matthew 16:8-11, Jesus rebukes the disciples for their little faith and inability to understand that His warning about leaven is about doctrine, not bread, showing faith is essential for spiritual discernment.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christ’s identity and divine revelation is taught in Matthew 16:16-17?
options: Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God, revealed by God the Father, not by human means
Jesus is a prophet revealed by popular opinion
Jesus is merely a wise teacher acknowledged by human reason
Jesus' messiahship is to be discerned only after his resurrection
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God, revealed by God the Father, not by human means
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:16-17 records Peter’s confession and Jesus' affirmation that this revelation comes from God the Father, highlighting divine revelation as the source of true knowledge about Christ.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Matthew 16:18 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 16:18, Jesus declares He will build His church and that the gates of hell shall not prevail against it, demonstrating His sovereign authority over the church and spiritual powers.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified in Jesus’ rebuke of Peter in Matthew 16:23?
questions.explanation: Jesus calls Peter 'Satan' and an offense because Peter’s thoughts are not aligned with God’s will (Matthew 16:23), showing God's holiness in opposing sin and temptation even from His closest followers.

questions.question: How does Matthew 16:21 connect to the broader biblical narrative of redemption?
options: It anticipates the Messianic suffering and resurrection as fulfillment of Old Testament prophecy
It introduces a new law to replace the Mosaic covenant
It presents Jesus as a political revolutionary
It denies the necessity of the resurrection
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the Messianic suffering and resurrection as fulfillment of Old Testament prophecy
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:21 begins Jesus' revelation of His suffering, death, and resurrection, which fulfills prophecies such as Isaiah 53 and underpins the redemptive work of Christ.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme does Matthew 16:28 anticipate?
options: The eschatological coming of the Son of Man in His kingdom
The immediate establishment of a political kingdom in Israel
The end of all suffering in this present age
questions.correctAnswer: The eschatological coming of the Son of Man in His kingdom
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:28 speaks of some witnessing the Son of Man’s coming in His kingdom, pointing forward to the eschatological fulfillment of God's kingdom.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 16:18 and 16:19 teach about the church's authority and foundation?
options: The church is built on the confession of Christ and wields binding and loosing authority from heaven
The church is founded on human tradition and has no spiritual authority
The church’s foundation is Peter alone, without reference to Christ
The church authority is limited to earthly governance only
questions.correctAnswer: The church is built on the confession of Christ and wields binding and loosing authority from heaven
questions.explanation: Verses 16:18-19 show Jesus building His church on Peter’s confession and giving him keys with authority to bind and loose, indicating divine foundation and delegated authority.

questions.question: What combined doctrine is taught by Matthew 16:24 and 16:25 about discipleship and salvation?
options: True discipleship requires self-denial and taking up the cross, and salvation involves losing one’s life for Christ to truly find it
Salvation is independent of discipleship and self-denial
Discipleship is primarily about earthly success and comfort
One can save their life by avoiding suffering and still be saved
questions.correctAnswer: True discipleship requires self-denial and taking up the cross, and salvation involves losing one’s life for Christ to truly find it
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:24-25 teaches that following Jesus means denying oneself and bearing the cross, and paradoxically, saving one’s life leads to loss, while losing it for Christ’s sake leads to true life.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 16:26 and 16:27 teach about the value of the soul and final judgment?
options: The soul's value surpasses worldly gain and the Son of Man will judge according to works
The soul can be exchanged for material wealth
Judgment will be based solely on faith without regard to works
questions.correctAnswer: The soul's value surpasses worldly gain and the Son of Man will judge according to works
questions.explanation: Verses 16:26-27 emphasize that no worldly gain compensates for losing one's soul, and that Christ will reward individuals according to their works at His coming.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Matthew 16:18-19 grants Peter exclusive, absolute authority over the church. What does the passage actually teach?
options: Peter is given authority as a leader through Christ’s foundation and the keys, but authority is exercised in submission to God’s will
Peter rules the church as an infallible pope without accountability
The church has no authority from Christ and is purely a human institution
The keys refer to literal keys to a building, not spiritual authority
questions.correctAnswer: Peter is given authority as a leader through Christ’s foundation and the keys, but authority is exercised in submission to God’s will
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:18-19 shows Jesus confers authority to Peter symbolized by the keys, but this authority is under God’s sovereign will and not an absolute, unchecked power.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin and hypocrisy is taught in Matthew 16:3-4?
options: Hypocrites can discern earthly signs but not spiritual signs, showing spiritual blindness
Hypocrisy is unrelated to discernment of signs
All people discern spiritual times equally
God gives signs indiscriminately to all who ask
questions.correctAnswer: Hypocrites can discern earthly signs but not spiritual signs, showing spiritual blindness
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:3-4 rebukes the Pharisees and Sadducees as hypocrites who can interpret weather signs but fail to discern the spiritual signs of the times, indicating sin-induced blindness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Jesus’ teaching about the coming judgment in Matthew 16:27?
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:27 emphasizes that the Son of Man will come in glory and reward each according to their works, demonstrating God's attribute of perfect justice.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does Matthew 16:13-16 have with Old Testament Messianic expectations?
options: Peter’s confession identifies Jesus as the Christ, fulfilling the awaited Messiah prophesied in the Old Testament
Jesus is identified as a new prophet replacing all Old Testament prophets
Messianic expectations are rejected in favor of a political leader
The Messiah is expected to be a priest only, not Son of God
questions.correctAnswer: Peter’s confession identifies Jesus as the Christ, fulfilling the awaited Messiah prophesied in the Old Testament
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:13-16 shows Peter’s confession that Jesus is the Christ, aligning with Old Testament prophecies about the coming Messiah.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 16:6 and 16:12 teach about the danger of false doctrine?
options: Jesus warns against the corrupting influence of Pharisaic and Sadducean doctrine, equating it to leaven
Leaven is only a physical concern and unrelated to doctrine
False doctrine is harmless and can be ignored
Only legalistic practices, not doctrines, are dangerous
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus warns against the corrupting influence of Pharisaic and Sadducean doctrine, equating it to leaven
questions.explanation: Verses 16:6 and 16:12 clarify Jesus’ warning to beware the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees, meaning their false teachings that corrupt faith and practice.
